My Tesla Model Y is the finest car in every respect I've ever owned. Most of the complaints here are ridiculous, and many are based upon issues in early models that have been corrected for about a decade.

Particularly the frequent-driver on the dangerous, icy mountain road is an absurd "case-study." The learning curve is NOT steep, and you have no business driving ANY car REPEATEDLY in what you know (repeatedly) are bad conditions unless you know how to operate crucial controls. Even more ridiculous about that "case-study" is that ALL of the main controls on modern Teslas respond to voice. You simply press the "talk" button on the steering wheel and release (very brief, and NO distraction), and then you SAY whatever you want: "Wipers auto," or, "wipers fast." And so on. It never fails. Never. I speak from almost a year of everyday experience. You can even open the glovebox the same way, and the glovebox security is, to my mind, a huge plus. Tesla's gloveboxes actually are secure, which cannot be said for those of other cars.

Now, to safety. Again, the icy mountain road "case-study" is an exercise in stupidity, with complaints about how dangerous the regenerative braking is in such conditions. Apparently people haven't bothered to do a shred of objective research. Countless reviews and many formal studies have shown that Tesla's braking and traction control is SO superior that you almost can't MAKE the car lose control BY TRYING in ice and snow conditions! It is far, FAR better than 99.99% of drivers at protecting you from loss of control, even when you are TRYING to lose control or are simply incompetent. The idea that regenerative braking is a hazard in bad conditions is flatly ridiculous, and I've tried it myself! On an icy/snowy parking lot, I accelerate to 50 MPH and just let off the accelerator entirely, fully engaging max regenerative braking. NO sliding whatsoever. I turn the wheel dramatically to one side at the same time. Traction control literally counters and keeps the car going straight with much less "sliding" than if I were in any other vehicle I've ever been in. I'm TRYING to make the car slide out of control, and I can't make it happen. These results have been objectively repeated in controlled studies in many conditions. In short, the Tesla is going to compensate for your incompetency BETTER than essentially ANY human can. And it reacts INSTANTLY, which is essentially infinitely faster than any human can.

I get that many people hate Musk. I get that there's an odd hatred of Tesla in some circles. I'm no fan of Musk either. But I try to make decisions based upon facts. And if we're talking about FACTS instead of prejudices, Tesla is an objectively superior car with an amazing balance of tech that is extremely thoughtfully designed. Of COURSE earlier models had growing pains, as do ALL new models of anything. But modern Teslas are an absolute marvel of engineering, and, again, hands down my Model Y is the finest vehicle of any sort I have owned. WELL worth the money.

And don't even get me started on how amazing the FSD is. Also well worth the money. I am now HAPPY to "drive" instead of fly, and there are fast supercharging stations everywhere. You can top off (adding 150 miles of range) in about 5-10 minutes, which is long enough to grab a drink and go to  the restroom. It's a nice break to stretch your legs for a few minutes, which is healthier anyway. Or, grab a meal and let the car fully charge in 30-40 minutes, giving you 300+ miles of range (at less than half the cost of gas per-mile!). And the relaxation of just letting the car flawlessly handle traffic and the monotonous sections of a trip are beyond description until you've experienced it for yourself. FSD is an absolute game-changer!

Oh, by the way, flush or recessed door handles are not a gimmick. Tesla designed the aerodynamics to be astoundingly slippery, putting the Model Y in the elite sub-0.22 Cd range shared by just five other vehicles, ALL of which have flush/recessed door handles.

All this complaining/carping, particularly about things like the door handles, prove nothing more than an effort TO complain and carp. I've owned my Model Y for almost a year now (and I am not offering this as some "compensated opinion"), and I would INSTANTLY buy this car all over again! There is simply NO comparison in the engineering/comfort/safety/luxury to price ratio to anything else out there. Again, this is my honest opinion having owned the Model Y for almost a year, and I get NO benefit from offering this opinion. I simply hate to see a video like this spewing STUPID and outright unfounded "critiques" based upon often decade-old "issues" that modern Teslas don't have. I am astounded that the Model Y is priced at a level that is actually attainable to the average person, and the bang-for-buck is all there.

I understand why a vehicle like the Tesla has all of these things integrated into its touch screen, and I don't even necessarily think it's all a bad idea, but it is horribly distracting when you have to make these kinds of adjustments when driving down the road.
